fix(release): run the REA audit on a Node.js the pin accepts

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"krovomi"} -->
_Requested by **Leub** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FcEdxXgpbM1pjjFZtdLjdJ?thread=cmsg_01FcEdxXgpbM1pjjFZtdLjdJ6exdLKzYphgErewBH4uiRV)_

## Base Branch

`main`, from `release/v1.6.0-node` = `main` (202ef118, tag v1.6.0) + one commit. `main` is merged back into `develop` afterwards.

## Description

The v1.6.0 Release run stopped on **build-macos-intel**, step "Audit what the packaged app exposes (REA)":

```
release-exposure-audit: rea-agents@6.9.0 needs Node.js ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1; this is v22.23.2
```

The four build jobs used `setup-node-frontend` with its default `'22'`, which takes whatever 22.x the runner image caches (22.23.2 on macOS). They now ask for `'^22.23.4'`, the first range of `apps/backend/rea/pin.json`. `tests/rea/test_rea_release_node.py` fails if a build job of `release.yml` asks for a Node.js outside the pin.

Once merged, Release is dispatched on `main` with `version=1.6.0`: the tag v1.6.0 stays where it is, the release is published on it.

## Type of Change

Release follow-up (CI fix).

## AI Disclosure

Written with Claude Code.

## CI/Testing Requirements

- Local: `tests/rea/test_rea_release_node.py` (red before the change, green after), `tests/rea/test_rea_frontend_pin.py`.
- The real check is the dispatched Release run.

## Breaking Changes

None.

+"""The release builds run the REA audit on a Node.js the pinned REA accepts.
+
+``release-exposure-audit.cjs`` refuses a Node.js outside ``pin.json``'s

001 T609: check-status-tooltip survives a window blur while the pointer rests on a pill

## What and why

`check-status-tooltip` (UI shard windows) failed on its first try twice on Windows CI (`hovering working shows the tooltip (no window blur, resize or scroll came)`, `a pointer event on a floor with no hint leaves the pill's tooltip shown`) and passed on the retry. Driver only, no app change. A hover does not need the OS focus (reproduced on Linux: the Working hover shows with the window blurred), so the focus ask is not the cause. A window blur clears the tooltip's pointer state (FR-187) while the pointer rests on the pill; a move inside the same pill sends no new pointerover, so the tooltip never returns, and a blur that came before osWatch starts is not counted: the Windows text. Fix: `hover()` leaves a resting pill first, the pointer step runs in `osRetry`, and the driver blurs the window (`H.forceBlur`, the shared helper: the blur is asserted on Linux and macOS, and on Windows, where a window keeps the focus on blur(), one `[focus]` skip line is printed and the step goes on) with the pointer on the pill before the first hover and before the pointer step, then asks for the focus by state. `TOOLTIP_BLUR=0` turns the blur off; mutant `TOOLTIP_MUTANT=noreenter` dies at `1440x900: hovering working shows the tooltip (no window blur, resize or scroll came)`.

Refs #2167 (check-status-tooltip)

## Spec and agent

- **Spec**: `specs/001-office-view-and-densities/` ([delta 2026-11-28](https://github.com/three-feathers/agent-durbar/blob/001-2167-status-tooltip-focus/specs/001-office-view-and-densities/spec.md))
- **Task(s)**: T609 (no FR)
- **Agent used**: Claude Code (vikramgorla)
- Existing capability reused (FR-031): `H.loseFocus`, `H.needFocus`, `osRetry`/`osWatch` of this driver; no new helper.

## Docs

Docs: n/a driver-only test change, no user-visible change (no changelog fragment).

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (321 suites; also test:force-blur, which now scans this driver) pass locally at 6868c51a5, no AI credits; `npm run pr:ready` ok; `npm run test:uisuite` ok.
- Driver on Linux (xvfb, DejaVu fonts): forced blur 5 of 5, TOOLTIP_BLUR=0 5 of 5; mutant noreenter dies at the text above. Reproduction before the fix: with the window blurred after a hover the pointer step failed with `shown before the pointer event (no window blur, resize or scroll came)`.
- Not verified: Windows itself (the condition is forced on Linux; a Windows window that loses the focus with no blur event is not shown here). The proof is the Windows shards' retry count after the merge. Simulator only.

Lint: LoopEdge holds the L2 badge's place for a step in state; cap 56 -> 50 (#625 item 5)

Part of #625 (item 5, the twelfth rule-by-rule follow-up; the item stays open). Scope set by Lumi: LoopEdge's six `react/refs` warnings, and two tests that pin the behaviour first.

**LoopEdge holds the L2 travelling badge's place for a step in state, set during render, instead of in a ref. The warnings go 56 → 50, and no `refs` warning is left in view. The rule stays a warning: one is left under a suppression comment. #625 item 5 stays open.**

## What the six warnings were

All six come from one ref, `planRef`.

At L2, in the full tier, the travelling `+N` badge stands in one of four places beside its token (docs/simulation-playback.md §PB4.8). The place comes from the badge plan (`badgePlaces`, cached per layout). It is read the first time a step needs it, and held for the whole step, keyed by `transition.fromStep`, per connection.

That one value decides three things:

- where the badge is drawn (`data-badge-side`);
- whether it is shown (`t3Clear`, its box clear of both end bodies);
- whether the connection's label dims under the token and badge.

| Line | What |
|---|---|
| 458 (two) | the ref read during render (`planRef.current.step`) |
| 459 | the ref written during render |
| 466, 611 | the held place passed to `badgeBoxAt` and `labelUnderToken` |
| 981 | the held place in the output (`side`) |

## What changes (`src/components/edges/LoopEdge.tsx`)

`planHeld` state replaces the ref. When a step first needs a place, it is read from the plan and set during render, and that render uses it. React renders the connection once more before it commits, and later renders of the step keep the place.

The key (the step number) and the scope (one per connection instance) are as before.

## What was compared (copies)

| | What | Lint | Mid-step layout change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1, this PR** | the place in state, set during render | 6 → 0, nothing new | the place is kept |
| P3 | no hold: the plan read on every render | 6 → 0, nothing new | **a travelling badge moved mid-step** |
| P4 | the hold moved into `badgePlanCache.ts`, one map for the app keyed by edge id and step | 6 → 0, nothing new | the place is kept |

- P3 breaks §PB4.8, so it was not taken.
- P4 was not taken: one map for the app could mix places across a remount or a document opened at the same step number with the same edge ids. That has not been measured.

## Measured cost, and its limits

- **Coffee roastery, zoom 1:** LoopEdge renders from step 4's start to τ 0.3 went 44 → 55, one more for each badge read at the step's start (probe copies).
- **MMO progression, zoom 0.8 (L2), 144 connections drawn:** real playback at 1200 ms a step, five steps a run, runs alternated main / P1 / main / P1, one worker, nothing else running on the machine.
  - Renders in a step's first two frames: **3 more per step** (288 / 304 / 328 / 448 / 448 → 291 / 307 / 330 / 451 / 451).
  - Frame intervals, means over the ten steps: mean 21.8 / 21.8 ms, p95 30.1 / 31.7 ms, max 113.4 / 116.7 ms; a step's first frame 18.3 / 19.9 ms.
  - **Limit:** inside one code, steps differ from one another by more than the two codes differ (the max ranges over 66.7–183.4 ms on both). These numbers do not show a difference, and they do not show that there is none.
- The timing-related specs (`playback-caps-perf`, `playback-ordering-timing`) passed in the 4-worker run below. That is not evidence about performance.

## Tests (`playback-badge-place`, two new)

| Test | before | P3 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| L2: a layout change in the middle of a step leaves each shown badge where its step put it | pass | **fail** (`e_roast_yield` down-right where up-left) | pass |
| L2: the step after a layout change reads the plan of the new layout | pass | pass | pass |
| the four existing tests | pass | pass | pass |

The second test's `down-right` is the place measured on the Coffee roastery at zoom 1, 1280 × 800, after Roasted bean stock moved 400 px down. The test says so.

## Checked

Related e2e, **4 workers**, no retries:

- Desktop (`chromium`): the 15 `playback-*` specs and `label-bends`, **130 passed**.
- Phone (`mobile`): `mobile`, `playback-visual`, `playback-a11y-background`, **88 passed**.
- `playback-visual`'s 3 screenshots were compared against the baselines, on desktop and on the phone, not updated: all match.

Also run: `npm run lint` (cap 50), `tsc -b`, the unit tests (5884 passed, 4 skipped) and all 26 `check:*` scripts pass.

## Warnings

- `npm run lint` fails above **50** warnings (was 56). Left: 50.
  - `only-export-components` 30, tracked in #712.
  - `set-state-in-effect` 20. RunStrip and TimetableRateChart stay the separate follow-up on #625 item 5.
  - `refs` 0 in view.
- **The `refs` rule stays a warning.** One `refs` warning remains under a `react-hooks` suppression comment, in `useDialogFocus`; it is one of the 18 hidden ones recorded on #625. The rule moves up when that one is dealt with.

test: wait for the aborted child to die instead of a fixed window

Closes #697

## Summary

The `windows-latest` CI job failed twice in a row on `main` at `tests/tui-shell.test.ts:222`: after aborting a `!cmd`, the test waited a fixed 400ms and then asserted the child process was gone. On a loaded runner the child was still alive at that moment ("Received function did not throw").

The production contract is met — `killProcessTree` (`src/tools/run-command.ts:79`) kills the tree with `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F` on Windows and with a process-group kill on POSIX. The race is in the test, which assumed a fixed deadline.

## RED evidence

- CI run `46099038607` (`main` at `66d6bbad`), attempt 1: `test (windows-latest)` → 1 fail, `tests/tui-shell.test.ts:222`, "Received function did not throw"; `test (ubuntu-latest)` → success.
- CI run `46099038607`, attempt 2 (re-run of the failed job): the same test failed the same way.
- The same tree passed in the pull-request CI run `46096498778` (`windows-latest`) and locally 5/5 runs — `git diff 2fe6297f 66d6bbad` is empty, so the production code is not the cause.
- The same test passed again on the next `main` push (`35ddc5c3`, windows-latest, 527ms), confirming a timing race rather than a deterministic failure.

## GREEN evidence

- `bun test tests/tui-shell.test.ts` → 31 pass, 0 fail (3 consecutive runs on the final commit).
- `bun test` → 3488 pass, 9 skip, 0 fail (3497 tests across 309 files).
- `bun run typecheck` → pass.

## What changed

`tests/tui-shell.test.ts` only (1 commit, 56 insertions, 11 deletions):

- the fixed 400ms sleep plus the single probe become a polling loop (100 probes, 50ms apart) that waits for the child to disappear, with a 5s budget;
- liveness is read through the repo's own `processAlive` helper (`src/file-lock.ts:20`), which treats `EPERM` as proof of life — a catch-all around `process.kill(pid, 0)` would read it as death and pass vacuously;
- the child publishes its PID atomically (write `child.pid.tmp`, then rename), and the reader polls up to 100 × 50ms until it gets a complete PID, parsed as digits only, so the probe never targets a truncated number, an exponent form or an unrelated process;
- the abort and the cleanup are armed before any assertion that can fail, so a failed test never leaves the shell or the child running;
- the test gets an explicit 30s timeout: the default 5s per-test timeout can expire inside the death poll, before the assertion and the cleanup, so a failing run could leave the child behind. The worst case is 5s to read the PID plus 5s to see it die, and the child's own 30s timer bounds any run that stretches past it.

## What I did

<!-- List the important changes: those that address the issue and need a reviewer's attention. Write one bullet per change, each on a single line. -->

- When stdin ends at one of its prompts, `create-storybook` now prints "Prompt aborted: stdin ended before an answer was received." and exits 1, instead of exiting 0 silently.
- The Playwright question at the end of init now follows the rest of the run: without a terminal on stdin and stdout, or in CI, it installs Playwright like `--yes` does, instead of asking after everything is already installed.

<details>
<summary>Detailed changes</summary>

<!-- Describe the changes more broadly: how the important changes work, plus supporting changes such as refactors, renames, and test or fixture updates. -->

### Two bugs behind one issue

**Exit 0 with no message.** The issue guesses that the stdin `end` listener from #36823 never fires. It does fire. I ran the published `11.0.0-beta.3` and `11.0.0-rc.1` in a real terminal with stdin from `/dev/null`, with a small preload that records stdin events and every `process.exit` call:

```
2250 ms  readline resumes stdin when "New to Storybook?" opens
2254 ms  stdin emits 'end'
2256 ms  process.exit(0)
           at onCancel (src/prompt-cancel.ts)
           at ClackPromptProvider.handleAbort
           at ClackPromptProvider.select
           at UserPreferencesCommand.promptNewUser
```

So the provider does its job and calls the prompt's `onCancel` with `'stdin-ended'`. The create flow's shared handler, `createPromptCancelOptions`, was written before that argument existed and ignores it. It records a user cancel in telemetry and exits 0 without printing anything. All ten create prompts that use it have the same hole, not only the onboarding one. A project that already has a `.storybook` folder and an empty directory both exit 0 the same way.

**Installs everything, then stops.** With stdout redirected, `UserPreferencesCommand` sees no terminal and answers its questions with the defaults, as `--yes` does. The Playwright confirm in `AddonConfigurationCommand` only skips itself for `--yes`, so it becomes the first and only question of the run, asked after `main.ts` is written and 104 packages are installed. In the trace, stdin is read for the first time about 47 seconds in, at that question.

The same cause gives three more cases the issue doesn't mention:

- stdout redirected but stdin a terminal (`npx create-storybook > setup.log`): the question goes into the log file and the run waits forever, after changing the project.
- `CI=true` without `--yes`: full install, then exit 1 at the same question.
- stdout a terminal and stdin closed, when the earlier questions are skipped (a saved "don't ask again" plus `--features`): full install, then exit 1.

### The fix

1. `createPromptCancelOptions` reads the reason. For `'stdin-ended'` it logs the same message the provider prints on its default path and exits 1, without counting a user cancel. Ctrl+C keeps its telemetry and its exit 0.
2. `AddonConfigurationCommand` asks about Playwright only when stdin and stdout are terminals and CI isn't set. That is the check `TypeScriptDependencyCommand` already uses, injected through the constructor the same way. Otherwise it takes the `--yes` path and installs Playwright, which is also the question's default. `cli-options.mdx` already promises this for init's TypeScript question: "init asks, or adds it with `--yes`, in CI and without a terminal".

Both changes stay in `create-storybook`. The prompt provider in core is untouched.

### Why not the other options

- **Let the provider handle `'stdin-ended'` itself and skip `onCancel`.** The sandbox, automigrate and minimum release age handlers all run on a closed stdin today and would change behavior, and #36823 passes the reason precisely so each caller can decide.
- **Throw from the handler instead of exiting.** `withTelemetry` treats a thrown error as a crash and can ask about crash reports, and that question then hits the closed stdin as well.
- **Skip the question inside `AddonVitestService.installPlaywright`.** That would also change `storybook add @storybook/addon-vitest`, where #36823 wants the loud abort.
- **Stop every run without a terminal unless `--yes` is passed.** That breaks runs that work today, like CI or a Docker build of a project that doesn't get the test addon.
- **Treat the whole run as `--yes` when there is no terminal.** `--yes` also skips the question that guards an existing `.storybook` folder, so init would run over an existing setup.
- **Check only stdout, like `UserPreferencesCommand` does.** The last case above would still ask on a closed stdin, after the install.

### What stays the same

In a terminal, the Playwright question is still asked and a "No" is still honored. Ctrl+C at any question still exits 0. Runs with `--yes` behave as before, and `storybook add` is not touched.

### Not changed here

React Native's Metro config questions are also asked after files are written and only skipped by `--yes`. A closed stdin only reaches them when the project type is passed with `--type` and the Metro setup is ambiguous, because otherwise the React Native variant question comes first, and that one now exits 1. I left them out to keep this focused.

### Tests

- `prompt-cancel.test.ts` (new): `'stdin-ended'` exits 1 with the message and tracks no cancel. `'cancel'` tracks the cancel and exits 0. The `process.exit` mock throws, so nothing after the exit can run.
- `AddonConfigurationCommand.test.ts`: the real terminal check decides the question. It is asked with both terminals, and skipped when stdin isn't a terminal, when stdout isn't, or in CI. The existing tests now inject an interactive terminal, like `TypeScriptDependencyCommand`'s tests do, so they keep their meaning in a test worker that has no TTY.

The four new cases fail on `next`.

</details>
